significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) predictive coupling that a measurable "coherence gap"—low or incorrectly signed alignment among representations of logically linked beliefs—forecasts self-contradiction and belief-vs-fact errors, together with the form-(ii) causal claim that a "propagation intervention" repairs both errors by restoring that alignment. This establishes both a behavioral phenomenon across entailment, negation, transitivity, and exclusion and a mechanistic account fixing expectations for unseen linked propositions; BeliefBank (Kassner et al., 2021) and MQuAKE (Zhong et al., 2023) illustrate why consistency and propagation across dependent statements affect belief maintenance and knowledge editing rather than merely one answer. True and false are distinguishable, although falsifying this conjunctive hypothesis would mainly rule out the proposed shared-subspace propagation account and would not identify which alternative mechanism explains incoherence. The topic-substitution check lowers no credit: deleting the specific alignment-error coupling and causal propagation mechanism leaves only generic research on internal LLM beliefs, which would not merit this score.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are explicitly named as the "coherence-gap" metric, its prediction of behavioral contradiction, and a "lightweight propagation intervention" that aligns linked-belief representations. The metric is potentially ex ante because activation alignment can flag a likely contradiction before the corresponding answer is produced, while the intervention supplies an action window for auditing or repair rather than merely explaining an observed failure. After per-model re-extraction, the claimed relationship still predicts that larger gaps yield more errors across several logical-relation types, so more than a direction-finding procedure survives recalibration; the hypothesis speaks broadly of "An LLM's belief," though its stated model-family and scale variation limits universality. The topic-substitution check confirms that this reach comes from the named predictor and repair handle—which could be used by model auditors or developers—not from the general importance of studying LLM beliefs.
